column1: # *** SO THE WHOLE URUGUAYAN INTERIOR HANGS FROM ONE COUPLE. ***
#   RAMON LERENA x MARIA JOSEFA GONZALEZ, of ROSARIO / COLLA, fathering children c.1800-1820
#     |- ALEJANDRO (b. Rosario; m. 1825 San Jose, Margarita Fernandez)
#     |     -> BERNABE - A TRINIDAD FATHER - and Carmelo Anselmo, Socorro, Pedro, Justina, Venancio
#     |- MANUEL LORENZO (b. 1812, Union, Montevideo)
#     |- LUIS MANUEL (b. 1820)
#     |- MAURICIO (b. Colla; m. 1837 San Jose, Casimira Montano)
#           -> CIPRIANO - A TRINIDAD FATHER - and Clara, Manuel, Ignacia, Belisario, Mauricio junior
# *** TWO OF THE SIX TRINIDAD FATHERS ARE NOW PLACED, AND THEY ARE FIRST COUSINS. *** Bernabe is
# Alejandro's son; Cipriano is Mauricio's; Alejandro and Mauricio are brothers.
# *** AND IT ACCOUNTS FOR ALL FOUR OF THE DEPARTMENTS THE CURRENT TREE POINTED AT. ***
# FLORES (Trinidad - Bernabe, Cipriano and the nest), SAN JOSE (both marriages, and Clara),
# FLORIDA (Mauricio junior, married there 1878), and now *** ROSARIO in COLONIA, which is not a fourth
# lead at all - IT IS WHERE THE FAMILY CAME FROM. *** The tree's fourth person is *** "Antonia Isabel
# Llerena GONZALEZ" of Rosario-Colonia ***, and GONZALEZ is Ramon's wife's surname. *** She is almost
# certainly another of their children. Not yet tested. ***
# ======================= AND NOW THE ANSWER ROW 138 ACTUALLY ASKED FOR =======================
# *** RAMON LERENA IS NOT A SON OF SANCHO. THE TWO FAMILIES DO NOT MEET. ***
# *** THE ARITHMETIC: *** Alejandro married in 1825, so he was born about 1800-1805. That puts his
# father RAMON's birth about *** 1775-1785. ***
# *** SANCHO was baptised about 1767 and married in JANUARY 1791. His first child, Pedro Antonio, was
# born in 1793. *** A man born in 1775-1785 *** cannot be the son of a man who married in 1791. ***
# *** Ramon is Sancho's CONTEMPORARY, roughly ten years his junior - not his descendant. ***
# *** WHAT THIS COSTS AND WHAT IT BUYS. ***
# *** IT COSTS the comfortable assumption that the Uruguayan Lerenas are one family. They are two ***,
# documented separately: SANCHO's, from Canelones 1791 into the Montevideo trunk of Lerena Lenguas and
# Lerena Traibel; and RAMON's, from Rosario-Colla across San Jose, Flores, Florida, Salto.
# *** IT BUYS a far better question than the one it closes. Sancho was "natural de Cordova la Llana".
# If Ramon was too, they are brothers or cousins, and the surname entered the Banda Oriental ONCE.
# If Ramon was born in the Banda Oriental, they are two arrivals and may be unrelated entirely. ***
# *** THE NEXT RUNG IS RAMON'S OWN MARRIAGE, about 1795-1810, most likely at ROSARIO in COLONIA or at
# SAN JOSE - and it will say where he was "natural de". That single phrase decides it. ***
# *** WHAT IT DOES NOT DO. *** It does not touch Pablo Armando. *** No Juan Carlos appears anywhere in
# this family, in any generation, in any of the searches that produced it. ***
